heading: PNG Compressor Online to Reduce File Size and Keep Transparency
introduction: Optimize PNG screenshots, diagrams and transparent artwork on your device. Start with Lossless for exact decoded pixels, or choose Smart, Maximum or Target Size when color changes are acceptable. Display dimensions stay unchanged.

sections.heading: What Is a PNG Compressor?
sections.body:
A PNG compressor is a tool that optimizes the way image data is stored in a PNG file. It can reduce unnecessary data and, depending on the selected method, reduce the number of colors used in the image.

PNG uses lossless compression at the file-format level. However, a PNG optimization process can also use color reduction. These are two different approaches.

Lossless optimization preserves the decoded image pixels. Color reduction changes image colors to create a smaller file, although transparency can still be preserved. FileCompresser provides separate options so you can choose the approach that suits your image.

sections.heading: How to Compress PNG Images Online
sections.body:
1. Select a PNG from your device and wait for validation.
2. Open Settings and review the PNG modes.
3. Keep Lossless, or choose Smart, Maximum or Target Size.
4. Choose Compress and wait for the result.
5. Use Compare and inspect text, edges and transparency.
6. Download a suitable result and keep your source.

The image tools preserve original display dimensions. There is no image resize control.

sections.heading: Understanding PNG Compression Modes
sections.body: Choosing a suitable mode is important because PNG images can contain different types of visual information.

sections.heading: Maximum
sections.body: Maximum is an optional color-reduction mode. Lossless is the default. Maximum can create a smaller PNG while preserving checked transparency values, but gradients, lettering and fine detail can change. Compare the result at its intended scale.

sections.heading: Lossless
sections.body:
Lossless mode preserves decoded image pixels. It is useful for screenshots, logos, diagrams and graphics where exact pixel appearance matters.

It may provide a smaller file through optimization of the stored data, but the result depends on the original PNG. Some images may already be efficient and show little or no reduction.

sections.heading: Smart
sections.body: Smart uses a more conservative approach to color reduction. It can be useful when you want to reduce the size of a PNG while keeping changes to visual detail under control. The actual result depends on the number of colors and complexity of the original image.

sections.heading: Target Size
sections.body:
Target Size attempts to create a PNG within a specified maximum file size. It tests actual encoded results and checks the final number of bytes.

The tool can report Target not met if the selected maximum cannot be reached. It is better to use a realistic target than to force an image into a size that makes its colors or details unsuitable.

sections.heading: Why Is PNG Useful for Transparent Images?
sections.body:
A transparent PNG can place a logo or graphic over different page colors without a solid background rectangle. PNG is useful for:

- Logos and interface icons.
- Product cutouts and illustrations.
- Screenshots, diagrams and charts.

The supported PNG modes preserve checked transparency values. Color-reduction modes can still change RGB colors, so inspect the result on both light and dark backgrounds.

sections.heading: Does PNG Compression Reduce Image Quality?
sections.body:
It depends on the selected mode.

Lossless mode preserves decoded pixels. Smart and Maximum may reduce the number of colors, which can change the appearance of gradients, text and detailed graphics.

Target Size may also use color reduction to reach the selected limit. Color-error checks act as safeguards, but they do not guarantee that every change will be invisible. For images containing small text, sharp lines or detailed illustrations, compare the processed version with the original before using it.

sections.heading: PNG Compression for Websites
sections.body:
PNG is commonly used for website graphics that need transparency or sharp edges. However, using large PNG files unnecessarily can increase the amount of data visitors need to download.

Website owners can review their PNG images and determine whether the format is still the best option. 

For example, a transparent logo may be suitable for PNG, while a photograph may work better in JPG or WebP. The right format depends on the image content and intended display.

If a PNG cannot reach the required file size, a supported WebP conversion may be another option. However, format conversion is a separate operation and may change image quality.

sections.heading: Are PNG dimensions preserved?
sections.body: The PNG compressor preserves the original display dimensions. It does not provide image resizing. If you need a different width or height, prepare a separate copy in an image editor before using this tool. Keep the full-size source for later work.

sections.heading: Private PNG Compression in Your Browser
sections.body:
FileCompresser processes selected images on your device. Your PNG files are not uploaded to the website's servers.

The tool accepts PNG files up to 50 MiB each. Queue limits are 500 files and 300 MiB total, while image dimensions are subject to the 32-megapixel limit. Your device's available memory can also affect processing.

sections.heading: Reduce PNG File Size with the Right Settings
sections.body: Choose Lossless when exact decoded pixels matter. Choose a color-reduction mode only when changes to colors are acceptable. Compare the actual bytes, transparency and visible detail before replacing an original.

links.label: Why some images do not get smaller

faq.q: Can I compress PNG without losing transparency?
faq.a: Yes. The supported PNG processing modes are designed to preserve transparency values.

faq.q: Does PNG Lossless reduce image quality?
faq.a: Lossless mode preserves decoded image pixels. It may not produce a smaller file for every image.

faq.q: Why is my PNG still large?
faq.a: Some PNG files already use efficient compression. Images with complex details and many colors may also be difficult to reduce.
You can use Target Size to attempt a maximum of 100 KB. Whether this is achievable depends on the image and selected processing options.

faq.q: Does the PNG compressor change image dimensions?
faq.a: No. The image tools preserve original display dimensions and do not offer resizing.
No. Processing runs directly in your browser.
